title: Batrim bar Yitas (Disputed Name)
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: In Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 3:3: Rabbi Acha bar Yitzchak entered to bathe with Rabbi Ba bar Mamal at “Batrim bar Yitas.” Korban HaEdah and Penei Moshe explain this as a person’s name. Arukh, entry Tar, however, quotes: “Rabbi Acha bar Yitzchak entered to bathe with Rabbi Abba bar Mamal in batrim,” explaining batrim as a Greek word for a bathhouse. The meaning is that they came to Bar Yitas’s bathhouse. In HeHalutz, תר״ם, the scholar יה״ש writes that it was a therapeutic bathhouse. Mavo HaYerushalmi writes that Batrim bar Yitas taught there; this is mistaken.

notes.text: The competing interpretations of batrim are Hyman’s report of the cited commentators and lexicon. תר״ם is read as Hebrew year [5]640. The scholar’s initials יה״ש remain unexpanded.

Guggenheimer Shabbat 3:3 reads bitreis bar Yitasas in the bathing account with Acha bar Yitzchak and Ba bar Mamal. The bathhouse-versus-person interpretation, Arukh wording and Greek claim, HeHalutz year and initials, and criticism of Mavo HaYerushalmi remain Hyman’s cited analysis; this digital occurrence does not establish a person named Batrim.
